## Natural history notes

A tiny freshwater amphipod characterized by a laterally compressed, shrimp-like body, curved posture, and small swimming legs used to move through vegetation and debris. In Florida, the Wakulla River Amphipod is known from the Wakulla River in northwestern Florida, where it occurs in freshwater spring-run habitat associated with submerged vegetation, organic debris, and clear flowing water. Like other Hyalella amphipods, it likely feeds on algae, biofilm, detritus, and decaying plant material, while serving as an important prey item for small fishes and other aquatic predators in the spring-fed river food web.
